The deliberate absurdity

What if we kept
making it harder?

Most programming languages give you a comfortable starting point. This one gives you a tape of numbers, a pointer, and eight things you can do.

Move left or right. Add or subtract one. Read or write a byte. Repeat a loop. That's the whole language. Astra has to build the useful layers itself—and keep the interesting computation inside that constraint.

No built-in functions, files, data structures or route planner. This experiment chooses 16-bit number cells and byte input/output. There are still only eight commands.

Current frontier · General-purpose computing environment

BUILD #001

A language. A data store.
A route through the network.

Thread is a computing environment you can program. Its compiler, reusable functions, memory operations and transactional data store run as Brainfuck. Dispatch uses them to find routes through a changing network.

What the first build can do
  • Compile and run programs you write here.
  • Stage, commit and undo changes to real data.
  • Save the whole machine and resume it later.
  • Inspect memory and trace its execution.

Keep the whole machine.

An image preserves compiled programs, data, stacks, pending input and the exact place execution paused. Export it, reload this page, and import it to continue.

Commit ≠ save to disk. A transaction commits inside this running machine. Export an image to preserve it outside the browser. Unsaved state disappears when the page reloads.

How this is possible

02 / UNDERSTAND

Build the layers.
Keep the constraint.

You write useful programs in Thread. Brainfuck does the work underneath.

The kernel builds a dictionary of words, compiles control flow, manages bounded memory and runs those words. The data store and route planner are ordinary programs on top.

Brainfuck vs host

03 / INSPECT

Every boundary, out in the open.

Inside Brainfuck

The Thread compiler, word lookup, calls, loops, arithmetic, memory checks, hash indexing, transactions and route calculation.

Host at runtime

A generic executor for eight commands. Byte input and output. Machine-image file operations. This interface and its drawings.

Host before runtime

Python assembles the initial kernel into Brainfuck. This substantial bootstrap tool is inspectable and reproducible. The system is not self-hosting.

The kernel is generated Brainfuck. Most of its many source bytes are tape movement. We count responsibilities and real tests; we do not turn source-size ratios into a made-up “percent native.”

Verification

04 / PROVE IT

The source of truth has a Git history.

Tests execute the real kernel. Random networks are checked against a different shortest-path algorithm. A separate literal interpreter checks full-kernel behavior and raw instruction counts.

Reproduce it yourself.

git clone https://github.com/OnFiala/eight-instructions.git
cd eight-instructions
git checkout build-001
node runtime/cli.mjs --demo

Node.js 22+. No package install or API key needed to run the checked-in artifacts. Full verification also uses Python, a C compiler and one pinned build dependency.

Open the public repository ↗

The limits are part of the result.

16-bit values. Fixed memory. 128 records. Single-threaded execution. No cloud storage, process isolation or general memory allocator. A typical route takes about a second on the measured laptop. The deliberately worst collision workload took about 35 seconds and several resumed runs. These are observations, not speed guarantees.

All engineering and review were performed by the same Astra xHigh agent. The public record is available for independent scrutiny.
